# Finding: the slot background is generated by the icon material

Answering `docs/superpowers/tasks/2026-08-09-find-the-slot-background-asset.md`, reported back to
session `818e0ae7-1f8a-4416-b485-6841c0a9ff2a`. Traced by six search agents over the installed
build, verified by a reconstruct agent and an adversarial refute agent, both against the original
screenshots recovered byte-exact from the session transcript.

## The answer

There is no background asset. The coloured background is computed inside the icon material
`/Game/ui/frontend/armory/armory_item_icon` (package
`fellowship/Content/ui/frontend/armory/armory_item_icon.uasset`) from three inputs it already has:

1. The item icon texture itself. Its RGB carries the item art over the baked neutral-grey backdrop,
   and its alpha is the inverted backdrop mask: 0 over the art, rising over the backdrop.
2. `GlowColor`, a vector parameter holding the rarity colour.
3. `UseGlow`, a scalar parameter that is 1 when the item supports the glow and 0 otherwise.

The compositing formula, confirmed to reconstruction accuracy below the screenshot's own noise
floor:

```
out = srgbEncode( lerp( srgbDecode(icon.rgb), srgbDecode(rarityHex), icon.a * UseGlow ) )
```

Source-over of the rarity colour through the icon's inverted alpha, computed in linear colour
space with alpha at full strength. With `UseGlow` 0 the icon draws as its plain grey self, which is
exactly what our current export shows.

The first session ruled out "source-over of any one colour through the icon's alpha" because the
test ran in sRGB byte space. The same blend in linear space is the answer. The 8288-vs-1306
distinct-colour argument for a separate layer counted RGB only; the alpha channel adds a second
independent per-pixel signal, and DXT5 compresses alpha separately from colour, so the tuple count
covers the observed colours.

## The material

`armory_item_icon` is a root `UMaterial`, MaterialDomain `MD_UI`, BlendMode `BLEND_Translucent`,
outputs EmissiveColor and Opacity (`PropertyConnectedMask` 3). Its full parameter interface is
three scalars `opacity` (1), `saturation` (1), `UseGlow` (0), three vectors `color` (white),
`GlowColor` (placeholder magenta), `RoundedRadii` (0,0,0,0), and one texture parameter named
`texture`. `CachedExpressionData.ReferencedTextures` holds exactly one entry, the design-time
default of `texture`; the import map holds four Engine material functions (`SplitComponents`,
`BreakOutFloat3Components`, `GetUserInterfaceUV`, `MakeFloat4`) and that one texture. A scan of all
44,371 content packages found nothing else that writes any of its parameters, so `opacity`,
`saturation`, `color` and `RoundedRadii` ship at their defaults permanently. The node graph is
cook-stripped (`Expressions` empty); the formula above was recovered by fitting against the game
render and surviving adversarial verification.

## The draw call

`W_ItemIcon` (`fellowship/Content/ui/frontend/armory/W_ItemIcon.uasset`) is not a composite widget.
`W_ItemIcon_C` derives from `/Script/fellowship.CRCommonLazyImage`, a `CommonLazyImage`, so it is a
single image whose brush resource is `armory_item_icon` at 128x128. Its ubergraph performs exactly
three material writes through the MID from `UMG.Image:GetDynamicMaterial`:

```
SetScalarParameterValue("UseGlow", SelectFloat(1, 0, OutSupportsGlow))
SetVectorParameterValue("GlowColor", CRBlueprintLibrary::ToLinearColor(raritySwitch))
SetMaterialTextureParamName("texture") + SetBrushFromLazyTexture(icon, bMatchSize=false)
```

`UW_GenericItemWidget.UpdateItemIcon(Target)` calls `Target.SetItemNew(CRItemViewModel.Rarity,
CRItemViewModel.ItemIcon, CRItemViewModel.SupportsGlow)` on both of its `W_ItemIcon_C` children,
`ItemIcon` (rendered) and `OnlyIconImage` (collapsed until `SetHideItemFrames` swaps them).
`SupportsGlow` originates in native code (`CRItemsBlueprintLibrary::GetIconForItemInstance` fills
it); the icons whose alpha is an inverted backdrop mask are the `CRVisualCollection` skin renders,
which is the same population the exporter already keys `discardAlpha` on.

## Where the rarity colour enters

The rarity byte switches over seven `CRNamedColor` class defaults on `W_ItemIcon_C`, each a
`NamedOverrideColor` row handle into `DT_DS_NamedColors_All`, converted by
`CRBlueprintLibrary::ToLinearColor` on the way into `GlowColor`:

| Rarity byte | Row | Hex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 Common | `game.rarity-common` | `DEDEDE` |
| 1 Uncommon | `game.rarity-uncommon` | `00E827` |
| 2 Rare | `game.rarity-rare` | `0070DD` |
| 3 Epic | `game.rarity-epic` | `A335EE` |
| 4 Champion (prints Heroic) | `game.game.rarity-champion` | `FFE565` |
| 5 Heroic (prints Regal) | `game.game.rarity-heroic` | `BE2525` |
| 6 Legendary | `game.rarity-legendary` | `FF8000` |

The doubled `game.game.` prefix on rows 4 and 5 is literal in the table's own row keys. The byte
order is evidenced by the two identical switch tables in the bytecode; the usmap carries no enum
names.

## Verification

Zero-free-parameter reconstruction of the game's 128x128 Legendary cloak render (item 5217,
`Icon_Warmaster_Cloak01_Legendary01_Back_R0_T0`), RMS in byte space over all pixels and channels:

| Model | RMS |
| --- | --- |
| Untouched icon (prior baseline) | 30.97 |
| Byte-space lerp toward `FF8000` (the first session's test) | 19.06 |
| Linear-space additive | 16.68 |
| Screenshot's own noise floor (alpha==0 pixels no model touches) | 11.78 |
| **Linear-space lerp toward `FF8000` by alpha** | **9.20** |

On flat pixels away from art edges the reconstruction lands within 1.8 to 2.9 byte levels. The
refute agent confirmed independently: a free 256-parameter alpha remap recovers the identity
mapping (so alpha is used straight); solving per pixel for the implied glow colour with nothing
assumed returns `FD7E01` to `FF7F01` across the clean alpha bands; the recovered glow shows no
drift against x, y, radius or icon luminance, so no vignette or `GetUserInterfaceUV` ramp exists in
the composite; an opacity sweep is optimal at exactly 1. The cross-rarity gate on the all-Regal
character sheet passed: backdrop pixels give median G-B of 0 as `BE2525`'s equal G and B require,
160 of 160 sampled pixels solve to a physical backdrop grey and alpha, and the one gold slot in the
same sheet matches `FF8000`'s chromaticity ratio (measured 3.60 to 3.68, predicted 3.63). The
remaining residual is chroma-only damage in the screenshot itself, proven by a chroma-only
transform improving the region no model touches. The measurement bounds the transfer curve near
gamma 2.2; the exact sRGB piecewise curve rests on how UE decodes sRGB textures in hardware.

## What export-all writes and the slot draws

- The exporter keeps writing the flat RGB icon PNG for the skin-render population, and additionally
  makes the alpha channel available to the consumer as the glow coverage mask. It must never be
  applied as transparency: used as opacity it erases the art by construction.
- The rarity hexes above ship with the vocabulary, keyed by the rarity ladder.
- The renderer draws the icon as `lerp(icon.rgb, rarityHex, icon.a)` per pixel in linear space,
  then encodes back to sRGB. CSS compositing operates in gamma space, so this needs canvas or WebGL
  math, or per-rarity variants precomposed at export time by the same formula.
- Items without the glow draw the icon RGB untouched.
- Slot geometry stays Slate-side: the `ItemIcon` instance draws the brush as RoundedBox with corner
  radius 10 at 128px scale (`RoundedRadii` in the material is dead; nothing writes it, and the
  blueprint's `SetRoundness` entry point stores a variable nothing reads).
- Layer paint order in `UW_GenericItemWidget`'s `ItemInfoOverlay`, bottom to top: `EmptyImage`,
  `ItemIcon`, `IsNewGlowImage`, `OutlineImage`, `RarityGlow`, `OuterFrameImage`,
  `HoverHighlightImage`, `ItemLevelText`, `StackCountText`, `IsNewIndicator`,
  `EmptyGemSocketImage`, gem socket content, `Image_UpgradeLEvel`. `RarityGlow` paints above the
  icon. `OutlineImage`, `RarityGlow` and `ItemLevelText` take the same `GetRarityColor` result in
  `OnRarityChanged`; the `SetOverrideColor` call in that handler tints `ItemLevelText`, a text
  widget.

## Method notes for future dissections

- The shipped usmap holds stub schemas for `CROverlay` and `CROverlaySlot` (no super, zero
  properties), which silently blanks `Slots` arrays and slot `Parent`/`Content`. Patching the two
  super links in memory before `LoadPackageAsync` restores them:
  `Patch("CROverlay","PanelWidget"); Patch("CROverlaySlot","OverlaySlot")` on
  `provider.MappingsContainer.MappingsForGame.Types`. Slot `Outer` fields in the export table
  confirm the containment without any schema.
- Cooked `UMaterial` keeps `CachedExpressionData` even though `Expressions` is stripped:
  `ReferencedTextures`, parameter names, defaults and `FunctionInfos` all survive, and the import
  map bounds the material's input set exactly.
- Any pixel test of a hypothesis about shader output belongs in linear space. The sRGB byte-space
  version of the correct formula scored 19.06 RMS and read as a refutation.
- The compiled formula for a stripped graph lives only in
  `fellowship/Content/ShaderArchive-fellowship-PCD3D_SM5-PCD3D_SM5.ushaderbytecode`; fitting
  against a native screenshot with the material's true inputs is the practical route.
